transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’ve been thinking a lot about whether my family would be better off if I just weren’t here anymore. My sister and my pastor got so deeply concerned when I talked like that, they jointly urged me to come in and get some help. I'm just so tired of everything.
Can you tell me more about these thoughts of not being here anymore, have you had any specific plans or intentions to harm yourself?

I've mostly just wished I could slip away in my sleep so my family wouldn't have to deal with me anymore. But on the really bad days, I've actually looked at my husband's extra insulin and thought about how easy it would be to use it on myself. It just feels like it would make things easier for everyone.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, energy, or interest in activities over the past few weeks, or has this feeling of being a burden been a persistent theme for you?

Yes, feeling like a burden has been constant for about nine months, ever since I crashed from a period of high energy. Now, I feel like I'm moving through wet cement and have completely lost interest in my quilting and gardening. I just feel like a terrible wife and mother, and this flat, hopeless mood hasn't let up since that crash.

Can you describe how your energy levels and interest in activities changed during that period of high energy, and how they compare to your current state, in terms of severity and impact on daily life?

During that high spell, I felt like I had an endless battery, running around from dawn until after midnight starting endless projects, but now I feel like I'm moving through wet cement and can't even look at my quilting or garden. It has completely ruined my ability to function; I've had to cancel all my quilting orders, step back from my church committees, and rely entirely on my sister and friends to manage the house and my husband's medical care.
Can you estimate how long that period of high energy lasted before you crashed, and have you had any similar episodes of high energy in the past?

I'm not quite sure of the exact duration, but that high-energy period felt like it went on for a few weeks or maybe a couple of months during this past year. I don't recall ever having any similar episodes of high energy in my past before this recent cycle started.
Can you clarify if you've experienced any periods of normal mood or energy between these episodes of high energy and the current low energy state, or has it been a continuous fluctuation?

No, there really haven't been any periods of normal mood or energy in between. It has just been a continuous, exhausting cycle where I went straight from that intense overdrive and irritability right into this deep, heavy crash. There hasn't been any normal baseline at all over these past nine months.

Have you experienced any distinct episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, lasting at least several days, where you didn't just feel more energetic but also perhaps more self-important, reckless, or easily distracted?

Yes, a few months ago I definitely had a phase where I swung from feeling on top of the world to flying into rages over tiny things, like someone being five minutes late. During that high spell, I felt incredibly self-important, truly believing I could single-handedly turn my quilting boutique into a national brand and fix all the historical society's problems. I completely brushed off anyone who tried to tell me to slow down because I thought I understood things so much better than they did.
Can you estimate how many days that episode of elevated mood, where you felt on top of the world and incredibly self-important, lasted?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of days it lasted because that whole period just felt like a fast-paced blur. I can't quite remember how long it went on before I finally crashed into this low.

Can you tell me if, during those episodes of high energy and feeling on top of the world, you also experienced any periods of depression or low mood immediately after, and if so, how they transitioned into each other?

Yes, right after that period of intense overdrive fell apart, I experienced a severe emotional crash into a deep, flat, and hopeless low. I went from running on an endless battery to suddenly feeling completely drained and hollow inside. Once that hit, I was left entirely unable to manage my basic responsibilities, and I just withdrew from everything.

Can you clarify if the episodes of high energy and irritability, where you felt on top of the world, lasted for at least 4 consecutive days, and if the depressive episodes that followed lasted for at least 2 weeks?

Yes, both of those periods lasted much longer than that. The high-energy phase was a continuous stretch that went on for weeks, if not a couple of months, a few months ago. And this heavy, hopeless feeling has been dragging on constantly for most of the past nine months since I crashed.

Have you experienced any other episodes similar to the one a few months ago, where you had a high-energy phase followed by a crash into a low mood, or was that a unique occurrence in your recent past?

No, this entire cycle of going into overdrive and then crashing is a very recent thing for me. It's been going on for about the past nine months, ever since my husband's health really started to decline. I have never experienced anything like this before in my life.
Can you confirm if you've had at least two episodes of these mood swings, from high energy and irritability to low mood, within the past year, or if this has been a single, prolonged cycle?

It has really been a single, continuous cycle over the last nine months rather than multiple separate episodes. It started with those first few months of me being in complete overdrive, and then I just collapsed into this deep, heavy low that I haven't been able to shake. It has just been one long, exhausting road since my husband's health declined.

To clarify, you've experienced one major cycle of high energy followed by a crash into a low mood over the past nine months, but have you had any smaller episodes or fluctuations within this larger cycle that lasted at least 4 consecutive days of elevated mood and 2 weeks of depressive mood?

I'm not really sure about smaller, specific cycles of those exact lengths. As far as I can recall, it has just felt like one continuous, intense period of overdrive that lasted a few months. After that, I completely crashed into this long, heavy low that I've been stuck in ever since.
Can you confirm if, during your periods of high energy, you experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, or if your thoughts and perceptions remained grounded in reality?

I didn't see or hear things that weren't there, but my thoughts definitely weren't entirely grounded in reality. I honestly believed I was chosen to single-handedly turn my small quilting boutique into a national brand and fix all the historical society's problems. I just brushed off anyone who tried to tell me to slow down because I thought I understood things so much better than they did.
During your periods of high energy, did you ever have thoughts or beliefs that were so unrealistic they seemed delusional, such as feeling invincible or having special powers?

Yes, looking back, those beliefs were definitely very unrealistic. I honestly felt like I was chosen to single-handedly turn my small quilting boutique into a national brand and solve all of the historical society's problems. I believed I understood things so much better than everyone else that I just brushed off anyone who tried to tell me to slow down.
During your periods of low mood, have you experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, or have your thoughts and perceptions remained grounded in reality?
No, I haven't experienced seeing or hearing things that aren't actually there. My mind doesn't play tricks on me like that, even when I'm feeling incredibly low and guilty.

During either your high-energy phases or your low moods, have you ever experienced any disorganized thinking or speech, such as rapid switching between ideas or difficulty maintaining a coherent conversation?

Yes, during those high-energy phases, my mind would jump so rapidly from one topic to another that it felt like TV channels constantly flipping. I also talked so fast and continuously about my plans that people at Bible study couldn't get a word in, even when I could see they were tired of listening.
Can you confirm if, during your current low mood, you have experienced any delusions, such as feeling guilty or worthless, to the extent that they seem unrealistic or interfere with your daily life?

Yes, I feel an overwhelming guilt all the time and constantly tell myself that I'm a terrible wife and mother. I truly believe that my husband wouldn't be so sick if I hadn't stressed him out with all my wild projects and business ideas. I just replay every mistake I've ever made until I feel like I don't even deserve my family anymore.

To confirm, you've had one major episode of high energy followed by a prolonged low mood, but can you clarify if you've had any shorter episodes of high energy or mood elevation that lasted less than 4 days, which might suggest a different pattern of mood swings?

I really don't recall having any of those short, brief bursts of high energy that lasted just a few days. I only remember that one major, prolonged period of running on overdrive for weeks and months before I eventually crashed.
Have you experienced any episodes of high energy or mood elevation that were not followed by a crash into a low mood, or have all your high-energy periods been followed by a low mood?

This is the only time in my life I've ever experienced that kind of high energy, and it absolutely ended in a severe emotional crash. I swung from feeling on top of the world and taking on endless projects straight into this flat, hopeless, and heavy low. It has just been that one continuous cycle over these last nine months.
Can you confirm whether you have had at least two distinct episodes of mood elevation, lasting at least 4 consecutive days, within the past year, or if this has been a single, prolonged episode?

As far as I can tell, it wasn't multiple separate high periods, but rather one single, continuous stretch of being in 'overdrive' that lasted for several months. That long period of high energy eventually led directly into the deep emotional crash I am currently experiencing.
During your current low mood, have you experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, in addition to your feelings of guilt and worthlessness?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't actually there, even when I'm feeling this low.

Can you confirm if you've had any periods where you felt slightly elevated or irritable, but not to the same extreme as your high-energy phase, and if so, how often these milder episodes occurred within the past year?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't noticed any separate, milder phases of high energy or irritability. I mostly just remember that major period where I went completely into high gear, and then the deep crash that followed.

Can you confirm if you've experienced at least one other episode of significant mood elevation or depression prior to the past nine months, or if this recent cycle has been your first experience with such extreme mood swings?

I don't recall ever having extreme mood swings or episodes like this before this past year. This whole cycle really seems to have started only after my husband's health declined and I took on so much of his care.
During your periods of high energy, did you experience any hallucinations or delusions that seemed to influence your behavior or decisions?

No, I didn't have any hallucinations like hearing or seeing things that weren't there. However, I did have very strong, unrealistic beliefs during those high periods, specifically feeling like I was uniquely chosen to single-handedly save the historical society and turn my quilting shop into a national brand. This absolutely drove my behavior, leading me to brush off anyone who tried to tell me to slow down because I thought I knew better.

Can you confirm whether you believe the current episode of low mood is part of a single, continuous cycle that started with the high-energy phase, or if you think you might have had any brief periods of recovery or normalization of mood in between?

Yes, I can confirm there were absolutely no normal or stable periods in between. I went straight from that high-energy overdrive phase into a sudden, deep crash, and I have remained in this heavy, hopeless low ever since.

Can you clarify if the duration and pattern of your high-energy and low-mood episodes, including the presence of any psychotic symptoms, align more closely with a pattern of distinct episodes of mania or hypomania followed by depression, or if they seem part of a single, prolonged cycle with fluctuations?

It felt like a very distinct shift where I had that high-energy phase of overdrive a few months ago, followed by a heavy crash into depression that has lasted for the last several months of this nine-month period. Regarding any psychotic symptoms, I didn't see or hear things, but I did have those highly inflated beliefs about being 'chosen' to fix the historical society and make my business a national brand.
Can you confirm if the high-energy phase you experienced lasted at least 7 days, which could help differentiate between two potential diagnoses?

Yes, it absolutely lasted much longer than just a week. That high-energy phase went on for several weeks, maybe even a couple of months, where I was constantly running around before I finally hit a wall and crashed. Just remembering how fast I was going back then makes me feel completely exhausted now.
Can you estimate the exact number of days or weeks your most recent high-energy phase lasted before you crashed into this low mood?
I really can't recall the exact number of days or weeks that it lasted. I just know it was a continuous stretch of complete overdrive a few months ago before I eventually crashed.
Can you confirm if your high-energy phases have consistently lasted at least 7 days, and if the depressive episodes that followed have lasted at least 2 weeks, to help clarify the diagnosis?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that. The high-energy phase was a continuous stretch that lasted for several weeks a few months ago, which is much longer than seven days. And this heavy, hopeless feeling has been going on for most of the past nine months, which is far longer than just two weeks.
